classification.difficultyReason: Divide a complete turn into twelve equal intervals and count the clockwise 150-degree displacement.

inlines.text: This regular 12-sided shape has a number at each vertex.
Ben turns the pointer from zero, clockwise through
Which number will the pointer now be at?

spec.sourceRegion: Question 13, polygon below the stem at the left
spec.description: Regular unfilled dodecagon, numbers 0 through 11 outside consecutive clockwise vertices, with 0 at left, 3 at top, 6 at right and 9 at bottom. Central pivot and left-pointing arrow toward 0. No turn arc or added angle label.
spec.mathematics: Vertex k lies at polar angle 180-30k degrees. The initial pointer runs from the centre toward vertex 0. Complete vertex labels use 10 pt.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the initial pointer is shown; no final pointer or answer highlight.
spec.sourceColourEvidence: Thin grey polygon, dark numerals and black pointer.
spec.shadingDecision: Unfilled polygon; structural black pivot and arrowhead only.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Angle per section} &= 360^\circ\div12\\\text{Angle per section} &= 30^\circ\\\text{Sections turned} &= 150^\circ\div30^\circ\\\text{Sections turned} &= 5\end{align*}$$
Five sections clockwise from 0 reaches number 5.
